w: Dug by hand 1666-1681 under Louis XIV's royal edict, this 240km waterway was Pierre-Paul Riquet's answer to linking the Atlantic and the Mediterranean without sailing round Spain. Built to shift wheat, not tourists -- renamed Canal du Midi by revolutionaries in 1789, one of Europe's oldest working canals.
_facts: 240km canal linking the Garonne to the Etang de Thau, part of the Canal des Deux Mers joining Atlantic to Mediterranean
built 1666-1681 under Pierre-Paul Riquet's direction, authorised by Jean-Baptiste Colbert's royal edict
originally named Canal Royal en Languedoc, renamed Canal du Midi by revolutionaries in 1789
one of the oldest canals in Europe still in operation
